final_hypotheses.title: p_m3n4 — Doggy daycare Mon–Fri; both work 9-to-5
final_hypotheses.prose: Both Hana and Priya work 9:00–17:00 office jobs. The dog (a medium-sized breed) goes to a daycare facility from 8:00 to 17:00 on weekdays. The 18:00 walkthrough: the dog is home (picked up at 17:00), which is why the dog bowl is on the kitchen floor and the toy is in the living room. Priya's entry items indicate she is arriving. On weekdays 8:00–17:00, the dog is OUT_OF_HOUSE (at daycare), so the dog bowl is empty, the leash is not used, and the dog food bag is not opened. On weekends, the dog is home all day: bowl is filled, leash is used for walks, toy is in active use. What sets this apart: the dog_bowl is empty (or the dog_toy is in storage) on weekday midday, and the dog_leash is OUT_OF_HOUSE on weekend mornings. What would refute it: finding the dog_toy in active use (on the floor near the dog) at 12:00 on a Tuesday, or finding the dog_leash in the house at 8:30 on a Saturday.

final_hypotheses.title: Dog home all day; midday feeding; both 9-to-5
final_hypotheses.prose: The parent (p_7c29) assumed the dog is at a daycare facility Monday through Friday, so the food bag stays sealed in the pantry and the toy is stowed on the storage shelf during work hours. The claim tally for the food bag has now turned against the parent twice: on two weekday-midday looks the bag was NOT in the pantry, which is hard to explain if the dog is away and nobody is opening the bag. This fork removes the daycare entirely. The dog is home all day and gets a midday meal around 11:00–12:00, which pulls the food bag to the kitchen floor. The toy stays on the living-room floor because the dog is here to play with it, and the bowl sits at the kitchen floor around the clock. Both residents still hold 9:00–17:00 office jobs, so their keys, phones, tablets, and jackets are out of the house during that window. What sets this apart from the parent: the dog food bag is at floor_k_k1 during weekday midday (not pantry), and the dog toy is on the living-room floor (not storage_shelf_s1). What would refute it: finding the food bag in the pantry AND the toy in storage simultaneously on a weekday at 12:00, or finding the dog leash at the entry hook on a weekday at 12:00 (no walk needed if the dog is already home and the resident is at work).

What would refute it: finding tablet_hana at desk_b1 or OUT_OF_HOUSE on a weekday at 10:00, or finding Priya's keys at the entry table on a weekday at 12:00.

final_hypotheses.title: Both work from home; midday cook then tidy; permanent counter fixtures
final_hypotheses.prose: Fork of p_d4e9. Three changes driven by the day-2 evidence. First, the recipe book block at counter_k1 (9–12 h) is removed: the claim scored 1-for / 2-against, and the per-object stats show the book in pantry_shelf_k1 on 1 of 3 sighted days with 2 empty looks at the counter during 9–17 h. The book stays in the pantry; it is pulled out only occasionally and not reliably at midday. Second, explicit "always here" blocks are added for the five permanent counter/table items (kettle, toaster, wall_clock, plant_pot_2 at counter_k1; fruit_bowl at kitchen_table_k1) that the robot has found in exactly one spot on every single sighted day (3/3) with zero misses during weekday 9–17 h. Third, a 14–17 h "tidy" block is added for the cookware and dishes: the 16:00 walkthrough on day 2 found pan, pot, plates, bowls, glasses, and mugs back in cupboard_k1 or drawer_k_k1, not at the sink. The cooking window (9–12 h) ends, dishes sit briefly at the sink (12–14 h), and by 14:00–17:00 everything is put away. The rest of the parent's structure (both WFH, keys/wallet/jacket at entry, dog home with pantry-stored food) is unchanged.

final_hypotheses.title: The kitchen counter is a permanent display; dishes cycle sink-then-cupboard
final_hypotheses.prose: This document isolates the "fixture" layer of the kitchen that no other document models explicitly. The counter_k1 is not a work surface that changes with the meal cycle; it is a permanent display shelf holding the kettle, toaster, wall clock, and plant_pot_2 every single day (3/3 sighted days, 3/3 weekday 9–17 h looks found them there, zero misses). The fruit_bowl_shared is likewise a permanent fixture on kitchen_table_k1 (3/3, 3/3). These items do not move for cooking, cleaning, or any other activity. What sets this document apart: it makes near-certain (almost_always) predictions for these five objects at all hours, and it models the dish/utensil cycle as a three-phase rotation—(1) 9–12 h: active use at sink_k1 during cooking, (2) 12–14 h: brief rest at sink_k1 or dish_rack_k1 while drying, (3) 14–19 h: stored in cupboard_k1, drawer_k_k1, or back on counter_k1. The day-2 16:00 walkthrough confirmed phase 3: pan, pot, plates, bowls, glasses, mugs, and spatula were all in cupboard or drawer, not at the sink. What would refute it: finding the kettle, toaster, or wall_clock anywhere other than counter_k1, or finding the fruit bowl off the kitchen table, at any hour on any day.

final_hypotheses.title: Dog food bag lives in the pantry; floor only at the three meal times
final_hypotheses.prose: This document refines the dog-feeding model. The per-object evidence shows dog_food_bag_shared in pantry_shelf_k1 on all 3 sighted days (3/3), with weekday 9–17 h looks at the pantry finding it 2 of 3 times (the one miss is presumably during the 11–12 h feeding when it is on the floor). The bag is a pantry resident that is briefly brought to the kitchen floor for the three daily meals (≈7:00, ≈11:30, ≈18:00) and immediately returned. Unlike p_d4e9, which gives the floor blocks "sometimes" and the pantry "usually" as a base, this document makes the pantry the near-certain default (almost_always) and narrows the floor appearances to tight 30-minute windows. The dog_bowl_shared, by contrast, is a permanent kitchen-floor fixture (2/3 sighted days at floor_k_k1, found 2/3 during 9–17 h) and is never moved to the pantry. What sets this apart: the dog_food_bag is almost_always in the pantry, and the floor blocks are narrow (7–7.5, 11.5–12, 18–18.5) rather than the wider 1-hour windows in p_d4e9. What would refute it: finding the dog food bag on the kitchen floor at 10:00 or 14:00 (outside any meal window), or finding it anywhere other than the pantry at 20:00.

final_hypotheses.title: Midday meal at the counter; two cooking windows; recipe book mobile
final_hypotheses.prose: Fresh document. The day-3 13:00 look revealed a cluster of objects in the kitchen that the existing "cooking 9–12 h" model does not explain: the dog bowl at counter_k1 (not floor_k_k1), the snack bowl at counter_k1 (not cupboard_k1), Priya's bowl at dish_rack_k1, Priya's phone at kitchen_table_k1 (not desk_b2), and Priya's glass at sink_k1 (not cupboard_k1). This pattern reads as a midday meal or substantial snack (12–14 h) at the kitchen table/counter, distinct from the morning cooking window. The day-2 20:00 look (cutting board and knife at sink, spatula at counter) confirms a second, evening kitchen window (18–21 h). The recipe book, seen in 3 receptacles and only 1/4 days in the pantry, is treated as mobile: at the counter during either cooking window, in the pantry otherwise. Hana works from home, alternating between desk_b1 and kitchen_table_k1; Priya works from home at desk_b2 but moves to the kitchen table for the midday meal. The dog is home all day; its bowl is at the floor by default but at the counter during the midday feeding that coincides with the meal. No objects leave the house on weekdays; the dog leash goes out on weekend walks.
